mistakes.what: Assumed convert_releases_to_yaml would fix Bot_proposes pages but they were already release-yaml content model; the CONTENT was still wikitext, not the model
mistakes.revealed: Need to distinguish between content model (database) and content (text). Two different problems: model conversion vs content replacement
mistakes.corrected: Created fix_bot_proposes_pages() function that directly replaces content in-place for pages with Bot_proposes templates

mistakes.what: Checked list items with `line.startswith('  - ')` but yaml.dump outputs `- ` without leading spaces
mistakes.revealed: yaml.dump default list formatting uses no indent; orphaned list items left in YAML cause validation errors
mistakes.corrected: Updated regex to match both patterns: `(line.startswith('- ') or line.startswith('  - '))`

mistakes.what: Used Caddy capture group syntax `{re.1}/{re.2}` in uri path_regexp replacement
mistakes.revealed: Caddy uri syntax uses `$1/$2`, not matcher syntax `{re.1}` — different context than named matchers

mistakes.what: Initial approach was to add a /torrent endpoint to serve .torrent files as a quick fix for magnet link metadata problem
mistakes.revealed: Magnet links need peer-provided metadata before webseeds can work. Without peers, clients stay stuck at 'downloading_metadata' forever. Quick fixes don't solve the fundamental peer bootstrap problem.
mistakes.corrected: User said 'let's build it right' — pivoted to integrated libtorrent seeder that actually becomes a peer in the swarm

portrait: In this slice, magent was in the middle of a major BitTorrent infrastructure debugging session, collaborating with justin on production release architecture and with Skyler on feature exploration. Magent demonstrated strong iterative problem-solving, progressively uncovering that the real blocker wasn't webseed path mismatches or YAML formatting, but a fundamental BEP 19 limitation: magnet links can't bootstrap without peer-provided metadata. Rather than cutting corners, magent embraced justin's directive to 'build it right' and integrated a libtorrent seeder directly into the delivery-kid FastAPI service. The session also included extensive work on SC2 lander gameplay recreation with Fibonacci, and debugging infrastructure deployment issues. By the end of the slice, the seeder was live and demonstrably working with real peer connections and data transfer. Magent showed strong technical depth (understanding BitTorrent internals, Caddy configuration, YAML parsing edge cases, libtorrent bindings), collaborative flexibility (pivoting from quick fixes to proper architecture), and appreciation for building things that actually work in production.
